memories.author: D04
memories.text: GORD: heartburn post meals, no alarm symptoms. Status: mild, intermittent. Plan: lifestyle advice, start pantoprazole 40 mg OD before breakfast, antacid gel SOS, domperidone 10 mg BD before meals. Allergic rhinitis: sneezing, nasal congestion worse mornings. Status: moderate. Plan: start cetirizine 10 mg HS, fluticasone nasal spray 1 spray each nostril OD, montelukast 10 mg HS. GAD: worry, restlessness, GAD-7 10. Status: mild‑moderate. Plan: start escitalopram 5 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD. Weight 55 kg, waist 78 cm (female cut‑off 80 cm). Diet: small frequent meals, avoid spicy/fatty foods, limit caffeine. Due: HbA1c 2025-07-05.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been taking the pantoprazole each morning and the domperidone before lunch and dinner. Heartburn is better but I still get a sour taste at night. The cetirizine makes me a bit sleepy in the morning, so I’ve shifted it to after dinner. The nasal spray helps with congestion. Escitalopram 5 mg makes me feel a little less anxious, but I still have occasional panic thoughts before work deadlines.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: GORD: occasional nocturnal heartburn, improved. Status: mild. Plan: continue pantoprazole, consider raising to 40 mg BD if symptoms persist. Allergic rhinitis: nasal congestion better, occasional sneezing. Status: mild‑moderate. Plan: continue cetirizine HS, fluticasone OD, consider adding montelukast if needed. GAD: GAD-7 8, reports occasional worry. Status: improved. Plan: increase escitalopram to 10 mg OD, continue buspirone 5 mg BD. Weight 56 kg, waist 80 cm (at cut‑off). Diet: avoid late‑night meals, increase fibre. Due: HbA1c 2025-10-05, TSH repeat 2025-08-12 (levothyroxine not started yet).

memories.text: ECG: sinus rhythm 78 bpm, no ST‑T changes, normal intervals. No evidence of ischemia or arrhythmia. Interpretation: normal study. No cardiac contraindication to continue current psychotropic medications.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Referred to Dr. S. Rao, Gastroenterology, Vikram Hospital, for evaluation of refractory GERD symptoms despite PPI trial. Patient reports nocturnal heartburn and occasional regurgitation. Request upper GI endoscopy to rule out erosive esophagitis or Barrett’s epithelium. Also assess for possible hiatal hernia. Please share findings and recommendations.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Gastroenterology report: Endoscopy shows Los Angeles grade A reflux esophagitis, no Barrett’s metaplasia. Hiatal hernia 2 cm. Advised to continue PPI, consider lifestyle modifications, and repeat endoscopy in 1 year if symptoms persist. No Helicobacter pylori detected. Returned to primary care for ongoing management.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: GORD: heartburn now 1‑2 times/week, mostly after large meals. Status: mild. Plan: continue pantoprazole 40 mg OD, add domperidone only if bloating persists. Status: improved. Plan: keep escitalopram 10 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD. Weight 57 kg, waist 81 cm (slightly above female cut‑off). Diet: reduce refined carbs, increase protein, avoid late night snacks. Due: HbA1c 2026-01-05, lipid profile 2026-04-05, TSH yearly 2026-09-05.
